nodes.summary: Let $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a substitution score and $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ a gap score. For all sequences $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$ and every valid alignment $A$ of $x$ and $y$, the score of $A$ with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$ is at most the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Needleman–Wunsch is optimal

nodes.summary: For every substitution score $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$, gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ and alignment $A$, the alignment obtained by listing the columns of $A$ in reverse order has the same score as $A$.
nodes.title: Reversal preserves alignment score

nodes.summary: Given a substitution score $\sigma$, which assigns an integer $\sigma(a, b)$ to all letters $a, b \in \alpha$, and a gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$, the score of an alignment $A$ over $\alpha$ is the sum, over all columns of $A$, of the score of the column with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$.
nodes.title: Score of an alignment

nodes.summary: An alignment over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a finite list of columns, where each column is a pair $(u, v)$ and each of $u$ and $v$ is either a letter of $\alpha$ or a gap.
nodes.title: Alignment

nodes.summary: Given a fuel $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and sequences $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, this lists alignments column by column from the front. With fuel $0$ the list is empty. With fuel $n + 1$: two empty sequences give the single empty alignment; if only $y$ is nonempty, with first letter $b$ and rest $y'$, each alignment of $x$ and $y'$ with fuel $n$ is preceded by the column pairing a gap with $b$; if only $x$ is nonempty,…
nodes.title: Fuel-bounded enumeration of alignments

nodes.summary: For sequences $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, this is the list produced by the fuel-bounded enumeration of alignments of $x$ and $y$ with fuel $|x| + |y| + 1$.
nodes.title: The list of all alignments

nodes.summary: Given a substitution score $\sigma$, which assigns an integer $\sigma(a, b)$ to all letters $a, b \in \alpha$, and a gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$, a column pairing letters $a$ and $b$ scores $\sigma(a, b)$, a column pairing a letter with a gap (on either side) scores $g$, and a column with a gap on both sides scores $0$.
nodes.title: Score of an alignment column

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a substitution score and $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ a gap score. For all sequences $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$ there is a valid alignment $A$ of $x$ and $y$ whose score with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$ equals the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Needleman–Wunsch is attained

nodes.summary: For a substitution score $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$, a gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ and sequences $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, there is a suffix pair $(x', y')$ of $x$ and $y$, that is, a suffix $x'$ of $x$ and a suffix $y'$ of $y$, whose Needleman–Wunsch score equals the suffix maximum of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: The suffix maximum is attained

nodes.summary: For sequences $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, the list of infix pairs of $x$ and $y$ is obtained by going through each prefix $p$ of $x$ and each prefix $q$ of $y$ and, for each such $(p, q)$, listing all pairs $(x', y')$ of a suffix $x'$ of $p$ and a suffix $y'$ of $q$.
nodes.title: Infix pairs

nodes.summary: If $A$ is an alignment of sequences $x$ and $y$ and $b$ is a letter, then $A$ followed by the column with a gap in the first row and $b$ in the second row is an alignment of $x$ and of $y$ followed by $b$.
nodes.title: Extending an alignment by a letter of the second sequence

nodes.summary: If $A$ is an alignment of sequences $x$ and $y$ and $a$ is a letter, then $A$ followed by the column with $a$ in the first row and a gap in the second row is an alignment of $x$ followed by $a$ and of $y$.
nodes.title: Extending an alignment by a letter of the first sequence

nodes.summary: If $A_1$ is an alignment of sequences $x_1$ and $y_1$, and $A_2$ is an alignment of sequences $x_2$ and $y_2$, then the concatenation of $A_1$ and $A_2$ is an alignment of the concatenation of $x_1$ and $x_2$ and the concatenation of $y_1$ and $y_2$.
nodes.title: Concatenation of alignments

nodes.summary: For a list of columns $A$ and sequences $x$ and $y$, $A$ is an alignment of the reversal of $x$ and the reversal of $y$ if and only if the reversal of $A$ (its columns in reverse order) is an alignment of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Reversing an alignment

nodes.summary: A list $A$ of columns, each a pair of optional letters, is an alignment of sequences $x$ and $y$ when no column has both entries empty, the letters present in the first entries of the columns, read in order, form $x$, and the letters present in the second entries, read in order, form $y$.
nodes.title: Valid alignment of two sequences

nodes.summary: For a list $l$ of integers, this is the largest of $0$ and the entries of $l$; in particular the empty list gives $0$.
nodes.title: Maximum of an integer list with floor zero

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be an integer-valued substitution score on letters and let $g$ be an integer gap score with $g \le 0$. Then for all sequences $x$ and $y$, the local score of $x$ and $y$ (the maximum Needleman–Wunsch score over pairs of infixes) equals their Smith–Waterman score (the maximum terminal-cell score over pairs of prefixes).
nodes.title: The local score equals the Smith–Waterman score

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be an integer substitution score, $g$ an integer gap score, $x$ and $y$ sequences and $c$ an integer. If the Needleman–Wunsch score of every pair $(x', y')$ with $x'$ an infix of $x$ and $y'$ an infix of $y$ is at most $c$, then the local score of $x$ and $y$ is at most $c$.
nodes.title: Upper bounds on the local score

nodes.summary: For an integer substitution score $\sigma$, an integer gap score $g$ and sequences $x$ and $y$, the local score of $x$ and $y$ is the maximum of the Needleman–Wunsch score of $(x', y')$ over all pairs of an infix $x'$ of $x$ and an infix $y'$ of $y$ (contiguous and possibly empty).
nodes.title: Local alignment score

nodes.summary: For sequences $x$ and $y$ and a list $A$ of columns, $A$ occurs in the enumerated list of all alignments of $x$ and $y$ if and only if $A$ is an alignment of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: The enumerated alignments are exactly the valid ones

nodes.summary: The cells `F[i+1][j+1], F[i+1][j+2], …` of a row from the remaining letters `b :: ys` of the second sequence, the remaining cells `up :: prev` of the previous row, the previous row's cell `diag` to the upper left and the cell `left` just computed. A previous row that is too short ends the row early (this does not happen for rows of the table, `nextRow_eq`).
nodes.title: Remaining cells of a Needleman–Wunsch table row

nodes.summary: From the row of the prefix `px`, `nextRow` computes the row of `px ++ [a]`: the cells `nwScore (px ++ [a]) py` for the prefixes `py` of `ys`, shortest first.
nodes.title: One row of the table

nodes.summary: The row of the table for the prefix extended by `a`, from the previous row: the first cell is one more gap than the previous row's first cell, then the recurrence left to right.
nodes.title: Next row of the Needleman–Wunsch table

nodes.summary: The rows of the table, filled top to bottom over the letters of the first sequence; the result is the last row. Row `0` is `F[0][j] = j * gap`.
nodes.title: Row-by-row filling of the Needleman–Wunsch table

nodes.summary: The last row of the table is `F[|xs|][j] = nwScore xs (ys.take j)`: the cells `nwScore xs py` over the prefixes `py` of `ys`, shortest first.
nodes.title: The last row of the table

nodes.summary: The last row `F[|xs|][·]` of the Needleman–Wunsch table.
nodes.title: Last row of the Needleman–Wunsch table

nodes.summary: Fix a substitution score $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ and a gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$, and write $|x|$ for the length of a sequence $x$ and $ax$ for the sequence with first element $a$ followed by $x$. For a fuel $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and sequences $x, y$ over $\alpha$, the value $N_n(x, y) \in \mathbb{Z}$ is defined by $N_0(x, y) = 0$, by $N_{n+1}(x, y) = g\,|y|$ if $x$ is empty and…
nodes.title: Fuel-bounded Needleman–Wunsch recursion

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a substitution score and $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ a gap score, and write $N(x, y)$ for the Needleman–Wunsch score of sequences $x, y$ over $\alpha$ with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$. For all letters $a, b \in \alpha$ and sequences $x, y$, writing $ax$ for the sequence with first element $a$ followed by $x$,
nodes.title: The Needleman–Wunsch recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a substitution score and $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ a gap score. If $(x', y')$ is an infix pair of sequences $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, that is, $x'$ is a suffix of a prefix of $x$ and $y'$ is a suffix of a prefix of $y$, then the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x'$ and $y'$ is at most the local score of $x$ and $y$, both with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$.
nodes.title: Infix pairs score at most the local score

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a substitution score, $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ a gap score, and write $N(x, y)$ for the Needleman–Wunsch score of sequences $x, y$ over $\alpha$ with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$. For all sequences $x, y$ and every letter $a \in \alpha$, writing $xa$ for $x$ with $a$ appended at the end, $N(x, y) + g \le N(xa, y)$.
nodes.title: Appending to the first sequence loses at most one gap

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a substitution score, $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ a gap score, and write $N(x, y)$ for the Needleman–Wunsch score of sequences $x, y$ over $\alpha$ with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$. For all sequences $x, y$ and every letter $b \in \alpha$, writing $yb$ for $y$ with $b$ appended at the end, $N(x, y) + g \le N(x, yb)$.
nodes.title: Appending to the second sequence loses at most one gap

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a substitution score and $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ a gap score. If $(x', y')$ is a suffix pair of sequences $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, that is, $x'$ is a suffix of $x$ and $y'$ is a suffix of $y$, then the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x'$ and $y'$ is at most the suffix maximum of $x$ and $y$, both with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$.
nodes.title: Suffix pairs score at most the suffix maximum

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a substitution score and $g \le 0$ a gap score. If $x'$ is a suffix of a sequence $x$ and $y'$ is a suffix of a sequence $y$ over $\alpha$, then the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x'$ and $y'$ is at most the terminal Smith–Waterman cell score of $x$ and $y$, both with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$.
nodes.title: Suffix pairs score at most the terminal Smith–Waterman cell

nodes.summary: For every substitution score $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$, gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ and sequence $y$ over $\alpha$ of length $|y|$, the Needleman–Wunsch score of the empty sequence and $y$ with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$ is $g\,|y|$: one gap per letter.
nodes.title: Aligning the empty sequence with a sequence

nodes.summary: For every substitution score $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$, gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ and sequence $x$ over $\alpha$ of length $|x|$, the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x$ and the empty sequence with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$ is $g\,|x|$: one gap per letter.
nodes.title: Aligning a sequence with the empty sequence

nodes.summary: Reversing both sequences preserves the optimal global score.
nodes.title: Needleman–Wunsch is reversal-invariant

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a substitution score and $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ a gap score, and write $N(x, y)$ for the Needleman–Wunsch score of sequences $x, y$ over $\alpha$ with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$. For all sequences $x, y$ and letters $a, b \in \alpha$, writing $xa$ for the sequence $x$ followed by the letter $a$,

nodes.title: Needleman–Wunsch score

nodes.summary: The table computes the optimal global alignment score (Needleman–Wunsch 1970), for every substitution score `σ` and gap score `gap`.
nodes.title: The table computes the optimal global alignment score

nodes.summary: Its last cell `F[|xs|][|ys|]`.
nodes.title: The Needleman–Wunsch table

nodes.summary: For lists $xs$ and $ys$, the list of all pairs $(p, q)$ where $p$ is a prefix of $xs$ and $q$ is a prefix of $ys$, the empty lists and $xs$, $ys$ themselves included.
nodes.title: Pairs of prefixes

nodes.summary: If a list $s$ is a suffix of a list $xs$, then for every element $a$, the list $s$ with $a$ appended at the end is a suffix of $xs$ with $a$ appended at the end.
nodes.title: Appending an element preserves suffixes

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score and $g \le 0$ an integer gap score. For all lists $xs$ and $ys$, the maximum Needleman–Wunsch score over all pairs of a suffix of $xs$ and a suffix of $ys$ is at most the terminal Smith–Waterman cell score of $xs$ and $ys$.
nodes.title: The suffix maximum is at most the terminal Smith–Waterman cell

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score, $g$ an integer gap score, $xs$ and $ys$ lists and $y$ an integer. If every pair $(u, v)$ with $u$ a suffix of $xs$ and $v$ a suffix of $ys$ has Needleman–Wunsch score at most $y$, then the maximum Needleman–Wunsch score over all such suffix pairs is at most $y$.
nodes.title: Upper bounds on the suffix maximum

nodes.summary: Given a substitution score $\sigma$ and an integer gap score $g$, the suffix maximum of lists $xs$ and $ys$ is the maximum of the Needleman–Wunsch scores of all pairs $(u, v)$ with $u$ a suffix of $xs$ and $v$ a suffix of $ys$.
nodes.title: Suffix maximum of Needleman–Wunsch scores

nodes.summary: If $s$ is a suffix of the list obtained by appending an element $a$ at the end of a list $xs$, then either $s$ is empty, or there is a suffix $s'$ of $xs$ such that $s$ is $s'$ with $a$ appended at the end.
nodes.title: Suffixes of a list with an element appended

nodes.summary: For lists $xs$ and $ys$, the list of all pairs $(u, v)$ where $u$ is a suffix of $xs$ and $v$ is a suffix of $ys$, the empty lists and $xs$, $ys$ themselves included.
nodes.title: Pairs of suffixes

nodes.summary: Fix a substitution score $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$ and a gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$, and write $ax$ for the sequence with first element $a$ followed by $x$. For a fuel $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and sequences $x, y$ over $\alpha$, the value $F_n(x, y) \in \mathbb{Z}$ is defined by $F_0(x, y) = 0$, by $F_{n+1}(x, y) = 0$ if $x$ or $y$ is empty, and by
nodes.title: Fuel-bounded Smith–Waterman recursion

nodes.summary: For a substitution score $\sigma$, a gap score $g \le 0$ and all sequences $x$ and $y$, the terminal Smith–Waterman cell $H(x, y)$ equals the maximum Needleman–Wunsch score over all pairs of a suffix of $x$ and a suffix of $y$ (the empty suffixes included).
nodes.title: For nonpositive gaps, the terminal Smith–Waterman cell is the best suffix-pair score

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score and $g$ a gap score, and for a sequence $s$ and a letter $c$ write $sc$ for $s$ followed by $c$. For all sequences $x$ and $y$ and all letters $a$ and $b$, the terminal Smith–Waterman cell $H$ satisfies
nodes.title: The Smith–Waterman recurrence

nodes.summary: For every substitution score $\sigma$, every gap score $g$ of either sign and all sequences $x$ and $y$, the terminal Smith–Waterman cell $H(x, y)$ is at most the maximum Needleman–Wunsch score over all pairs of a suffix of $x$ and a suffix of $y$.
nodes.title: The terminal cell is at most the suffix maximum

nodes.summary: For a substitution score $\sigma$, a gap score $g$, sequences $x$ and $y$, a prefix $p$ of $x$ and a prefix $q$ of $y$, the terminal Smith–Waterman cell $H(p, q)$ is at most the Smith–Waterman score of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Each prefix-pair cell is at most the Smith–Waterman score

nodes.summary: For a substitution score $\sigma$, a gap score $g$ and every sequence $y$, the terminal Smith–Waterman cell of the empty sequence and $y$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The terminal cell vanishes when the first sequence is empty

nodes.summary: For a substitution score $\sigma$, a gap score $g$ and every sequence $x$, the terminal Smith–Waterman cell of $x$ and the empty sequence is $0$.
nodes.title: The terminal cell vanishes when the second sequence is empty

nodes.summary: For every substitution score $\sigma$, every gap score $g$ and all sequences $x$ and $y$, the terminal Smith–Waterman cell $H(x, y)$ satisfies $H(x, y) \ge 0$.
nodes.title: The terminal Smith–Waterman cell is nonnegative

nodes.summary: Given a substitution score $\sigma(a, b) \in \mathbb{Z}$ for letters $a, b$ and a gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$, and writing $sc$ for a sequence $s$ followed by a letter $c$, the terminal Smith–Waterman cell $H(x, y)$ of two sequences $x$ and $y$ is the integer defined by $H(x, y) = 0$ when $x$ or $y$ is empty, and
nodes.title: The terminal Smith–Waterman cell

nodes.summary: For a substitution score $\sigma$, a gap score $g$, sequences $x$ and $y$ and an integer $c$, if the terminal Smith–Waterman cell $H(p, q)$ is at most $c$ for every prefix $p$ of $x$ and every prefix $q$ of $y$, then the Smith–Waterman score of $x$ and $y$ is at most $c$.
nodes.title: Bounding the Smith–Waterman score by its cells

nodes.summary: Given a substitution score $\sigma$ and a gap score $g$, the Smith–Waterman score of two sequences $x$ and $y$ is the maximum of the terminal Smith–Waterman cell $H(p, q)$ over all pairs of a prefix $p$ of $x$ and a prefix $q$ of $y$ (the empty prefixes included).
nodes.title: The Smith–Waterman score

nodes.summary: For every scoring function $\sigma : \alpha \to \alpha \to \mathbb{Z}$, every gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$ and all lists $x$ and $y$ over $\alpha$, the suffix maximum of $x$ and $y$ (the largest Needleman–Wunsch score, under $\sigma$ and $g$, of a suffix of $x$ against a suffix of $y$) is at least $0$, since the pair of empty suffixes scores $0$.
nodes.title: The suffix maximum is nonnegative

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
